wp: WP4 Branching and data directory (bind mounts, reflink fork, pg_basebackup fallback, volume fork, managed-db data dirs, legacy migration, teardown, #34 readiness)
summary:
Today every byte of branch state lives in Docker-managed volumes: the Postgres container is `docker run` with no `-v` (src/adapters/postgres.ts:15-17), so PGDATA is an anonymous volume from the image's `VOLUME /var/lib/postgresql/data` (verified on postgres:16-alpine); compute /data is a named volume `io-<ref>-data-<volId>` (src/adapters/compute.ts:23, src/engine.ts:235); managed DBs write into anonymous volumes too (src/adapters/manageddb.ts:14-15). A branch clone is `pg_dump` buffered in the daemon then `psql` (postgres.ts:28-31), O(data), and the clone's volume is born empty (engine.ts:216-218). Readiness is `pg_isready` over the unix socket (postgres.ts:37-43), which is true during the image's init-time temporary server and is the #34 race. `docker rm -f` without `-v` (postgres.ts:34, compute.ts:38) leaks anonymous volumes.

Target: one data directory (`INSTA_OSS_DATA_DIR`, a HOST path, default `~/.insta-oss` local / `/var/lib/instacloud` server, mounted at the same path inside the daemon container in server mode) with an immutable-id layout `pg/<ref>/<svcKey>`, `vol/<ref>/<volId>`, `md/<ref>/<prefix>-<dataId>`, bind-mounted into the containers. A new `src/datadir.ts` (DataDir: layout, boot probe, copy engines, remove) plus a dependency-free `src/fsclone.cjs` copy program that runs in-process (server mode as root, macOS) or inside a throwaway `node:22-alpine` container when the daemon cannot read uid-999 data (unprivileged Linux local mode). Postgres fork = `CHECKPOINT` on a live source (skipped when the source is at rest), then an ordered reflink copy (pg_control snapshot FIRST, everything else, `pg_wal` LAST, pg_basebackup's exclusion list scrubbed, postmaster.pid removed), start the clone container on the copy, TCP readiness with retry-on-connect; a failed recovery retries once then falls back to streaming `pg_basebackup -X stream` from a throwaway container over the branch network (needs one `host replication` pg_hba line the adapter appends at provision). Volumes fork with the same copy engine. Managed DBs stay fresh and empty per branch (cloud parity, insta-platform services.ts:873-874) but their data moves to bind mounts. Teardown removes directories after containers. A one-time boot migration moves legacy volume state into the layout with `--volumes-from` copies and stamps `Branch.dataVersion = 1`. No new route; POST /projects/:id/branches changes only in how it does the work. Fake-adapter contract tests grow (fork call order, host paths, teardown removals, migration plan, retry-on-connect, fsclone unit tests); Docker tests (integrator only) cover fork timing and size independence, sleeping-source fork, volume fork, migration, and TCP readiness.

files.change: NEW (shared with WP1/WP2/WP3; reconciler merges). Reads INSTA_OSS_MODE ('local'|'server', default local), INSTA_OSS_DATA_DIR (host path; default join(homedir(),'.insta-oss') in local, '/var/lib/instacloud' in server), INSTA_OSS_HELPER_IMAGE (default 'node:22-alpine'), INSTA_OSS_FORK ('auto'|'reflink'|'basebackup', default auto), INSTA_OSS_DATA_MIGRATE ('1' default; '0' skips the boot migration, tests only). Exports `config` and `layout(dataDir)`. Keeps INSTA_OSS_STATE (state.ts:17) as is.

NEW. `DataDirOps` interface + `DataDir` class: layout helpers (pg/vol/md/branchRoots/probe paths), `probe()` at boot (mkdir -p, fs.copyFileSync with COPYFILE_FICLONE_FORCE on a 1 MiB temp file; catches ENOTSUP/EXDEV/EINVAL -> reflink=false; also records canRead = whether an EACCES-free stat of an existing 0700 uid-999 dir is possible, i.e. process.getuid()===0 || platform==='darwin'), `ensureDir(path, mode)`, `assertPgData(dir)` (PG_VERSION must exist), `assertEmptyOrMissing(dir)`, `clonePostgres(src, dst)` (ordered reflink copy, see algorithm), `cloneTree(src, dst)` (volume fork), `remove(path)`, `copyFromVolumes(container|volumeName, containerPath, dst)` (migration). Each op runs in-process first and re-runs inside the helper container on EACCES (Linux only), piping src/fsclone.cjs on stdin via docker(['run','--rm','-i','-v',`${dataDir}:${dataDir}`, helperImage,'node','-', ...args], {input}).

NEW, plain CommonJS, node built-ins only (fs, path), no imports from src/. Verbs: `probe <dir>`, `clone <src> <dst> --reflink=always|auto [--pg]`, `rm <path>`. Implements the recursive walker (mkdir+chmod, copyFile with COPYFILE_FICLONE_FORCE or fallback, symlink recreate, lchown when uid 0, utimes), the Postgres ordering and scrub list under --pg, and exits non-zero with the errno on failure. Required by src/datadir.ts in-process and streamed to the helper container. Add to eslint config as a CommonJS file.

Bind mount `-v <dataDir>:/var/lib/postgresql/data` in provision (replaces the anonymous volume, :15-17); provision asserts the dir is empty or missing before initdb; appends the `host replication all all scram-sha-256  # insta-oss basebackup` pg_hba line + pg_reload_conf after readiness; `fork(src, dst)` implements CHECKPOINT -> DataDir.clonePostgres -> run container -> readiness -> scrub/retry -> basebackup fallback and returns {url, method, ms}; `waitReady` moves to TCP (`pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1` then `psql -h 127.0.0.1 -c 'select 1'`) with a deadline (fixes #34); `query` gains retry-on-connect (matches 'server closed the connection unexpectedly', 'Connection refused', 'the database system is starting up', 'is not currently accepting connections'; 500 ms backoff, 30 s deadline; other errors surface immediately); `destroy` becomes `docker rm -f -v` (:34) and removes only the container (the engine removes the directory); `cloneInto` deleted. Constructor takes DataDirOps.

`volume?: { hostPath: string }` replaces `{ name }` (:14, :23): `-v <hostPath>:/data`; `destroy` uses `docker rm -f -v` and no longer sweeps named volumes (:41-42, the engine removes vol/<ref>). No other change here (the `-p` removal is WP2's).

Catalog gains `dataPaths: Array<{ container: string; sub: string }>` per type: redis [{'/data','data'}], mysql [{'/var/lib/mysql','mysql'}], mongodb [{'/data/db','db'},{'/data/configdb','configdb'}] (the image VOLUME paths; valkey --dir /data is at :31).
`provision(..., opts: { dataDir })` mounts each catalog dataPath as `-v <dataDir>/<sub>:<container>`; `destroy` uses `rm -f -v`; rename unchanged (dir is keyed by dataId so nothing on disk moves).

DatabaseAdapter: provision(ref, network, opts:{dataDir}), fork(src:{ref,url,dataDir}, dst:{ref,network,dataDir}) -> {url, method, ms}, destroy container-only, cloneInto removed (:89-94). ComputeAdapter.deploy volume?: { hostPath } (:112). ManagedDbAdapter.provision(..., opts:{dataDir}) (:128). Branch.dataVersion?: 1 (:41-67). Project.managedServices[].dataId?: string (:34). New exported `DataDirOps` type re-exported from datadir.ts (or defined here) so the Engine can be constructed with a fake.

Constructor gains `data: DataDirOps` (5th arg, default `new DataDir(config)`). provisionBranch(project, name, isDefault, source: Branch | null): db step = provision (source null) or fork (source given; url derived from source.dbUrl), then storage, then managed (dirs created per dataId), then dataVersion:1 on the row; compensation removes dirs. createBranch: mark src+dst refs in flight, fork db, fork every compute volume (`data.cloneTree(vol/<src>/<id>, vol/<dst>/<id>)`) BEFORE the redeploy loop (:139-141), storage.cloneInto unchanged, event payload `{ from, db:{method,ms}, volumes:[{group,method,ms}] }`. deployLocked passes `volume: { hostPath: layout.vol(ref, vol.id) }` after `data.ensureDir(path, 0o777)` (:235). removeComputeService/removeServiceVolume: `data.remove(vol/<ref>/<id>)` replaces `docker volume rm` (:833, :1006). destroyBranch/destroyProject: after container destroys, `data.remove` each of pg/<ref>, vol/<ref>, md/<ref> (:1141-1169). addManagedService mints dataId; managedRow/rename untouched. New `migrateLegacyData()` (called from main) and `dataCapabilities()` getter for logs.

NEW. One-time migration of branches with `dataVersion === undefined`: per branch, per resource, stop -> `--volumes-from` copy into the layout -> `docker rm -v` -> recreate with bind mounts -> restore run state -> stamp. Idempotent and resumable (a resource whose target dir already holds data is skipped). Called by main.ts before the router/scheduler start.

Boot order: config -> docker check (:16-17) -> `DataDir.probe()` (log one line: path, reflink yes/no, copy engine, mode) -> `migrateLegacyData()` unless INSTA_OSS_DATA_MIGRATE=0 -> construct adapters with the DataDir -> listen (:19-21). Adapters get the DataDir instance.

Fake db adapter: replace `cloneInto` with `fork` recording `db.fork:<src>-><dst>` and returning `{ url: 'pg://<dst>', method: 'reflink', ms: 1 }`; provision records `db.provision:<ref>`; add a fake DataDirOps recording `data.clone:<src>-><dst>`, `data.remove:<path>`, `data.ensure:<path>`. Update :126 (db.clone -> db.fork), :783/:833 (volume name -> host path `.../vol/demo-main/<id>`), :1272 (branch create no longer provisions the db). New tests listed under tests.
NEW unit tests for src/fsclone.cjs and DataDir on a tmp dir (no Docker).
NEW unit tests with docker mocked (like test/restart-policy.test.ts): bind-mount args, TCP readiness args, retry-on-connect, fork call sequence and basebackup fallback trigger.
NEW unit test with docker mocked: legacy state (no dataVersion) produces the exact docker call plan and stamps dataVersion.
NEW Docker test (integrator only): fork timing, size independence, sleeping source, volume fork, teardown removes dirs.
NEW Docker test (integrator only): hand-built legacy containers migrate into the layout with data intact.
Set INSTA_OSS_DATA_DIR to a realpath'd tmp dir in beforeAll (:18-20); assert the branch.created event carries db.method; keep the isolation assertions.
provision now takes opts {dataDir} (:41); assert `-v <dataDir>:/var/lib/postgresql/data` is present.

Add a step before `npm test`: create a 4 GiB XFS reflink loop image (`fallocate`, `mkfs.xfs -m reflink=1`, `sudo mount -o loop`, chown to runner) and export INSTA_OSS_DATA_DIR to it so the reflink path runs on ubuntu-latest (ext4 root would otherwise always take the basebackup path); a second `npx vitest run test/fork.int.test.ts` with INSTA_OSS_FORK=basebackup covers the fallback.

Line 23 (volume 'Same size, empty') and line 54 (self-host = dump-and-restore) become: self-hosted Postgres and /data volumes fork at the file level on a reflink filesystem (sub-second, any size); managed DBs stay fresh. No em dashes.
Lines 17 and 20 same edit as above.
Add a 'Data directory' section: path, reflink requirement, what happens without it, migration on first boot.
`branch create` row: 'create = fork: file-level copy of the database and /data volumes (reflink), bucket copy, app redeploy'.
Code map: add datadir.ts, fsclone.cjs, datadir-migrate.ts; postgres.ts line 'clone = reflink fork, pg_basebackup fallback'; test list additions.

sharedSurface.config:
Read by this WP (src/config.ts, shared):
- INSTA_OSS_MODE = 'local' | 'server' (default 'local').
- INSTA_OSS_DATA_DIR: HOST path. Default local: join(homedir(), '.insta-oss') (same dir as state.json today, state.ts:17); server: '/var/lib/instacloud'. Invariant: in server mode the compose file mounts this path at the SAME path inside the daemon container (docker -v uses host paths). On macOS it must be under a Docker Desktop shared location (~ is).
- INSTA_OSS_HELPER_IMAGE (default 'node:22-alpine'): only pulled when the daemon cannot read the data dir in-process (unprivileged Linux local mode). Justification for the image (not an npm dep): runs the same src/fsclone.cjs as root inside the mount; no coreutils dependency in the daemon image (alpine busybox cp has no --reflink, verified on postgres:16-alpine).
- INSTA_OSS_FORK = 'auto' | 'reflink' | 'basebackup' (default auto): 'basebackup' forces the fallback (CI coverage); 'reflink' fails loudly instead of falling back (installer smoke test).
- INSTA_OSS_DATA_MIGRATE = '1' | '0' (default 1): skip the boot migration (tests).
Introduced layout (function of dataDir, never stored in state):
  <dataDir>/pg/<ref>/<svcKey>            svcKey = 'db' for today's fixed pg-db (engine.ts:434); a multi-postgres WP mints immutable keys per service
  <dataDir>/vol/<ref>/<volId>            volId = Project.computeVolumes[group].id (engine.ts:780), already immutable across renames (engine.ts:807-810)
  <dataDir>/md/<ref>/<idPrefix>-<dataId>/<sub>   sub per catalog dataPaths (redis data; mysql mysql; mongodb db, configdb)
  <dataDir>/.probe/                       boot probe scratch
Rule: directories are keyed by immutable ids, never by user-renamable names, because `docker start` re-binds by the stored host path and docker silently creates a missing bind source as an empty dir (a renamed dir would look like data loss on the next wake).
Installer contract (WP1): <dataDir> exists, mode 0700 root, on a reflink filesystem (XFS reflink=1, btrfs, or the loop-mounted XFS image), mounted at the same path in the daemon container, daemon runs as uid 0 in its container.
sharedSurface.engineSeams:
- Engine.provisionBranch(project, name, isDefault, source: Branch | null) replaces (…, cloneOf: string|null) (engine.ts:66). createBranch passes the source Branch; createProject passes null.
- Engine.createBranch (engine.ts:128-152): new order = provisionBranch(fork db, provision storage, provision managed) -> fork volumes -> storage.cloneInto -> redeploy loop -> secrets/dbVolumeGib copy -> emit. Used by WP2 (hostnames in dbUrl: the adapter builds the clone URL from the SOURCE url with only the host swapped, so whatever host shape WP2 mints is preserved) and WP5 (template deploys reuse deployLocked's volume path).
- Engine.ops (WP3 seam): `opsInFlight: Set<string>` of refs; createBranch adds src and dst refs for the duration so the sweep/eviction never stops the source mid-basebackup or the clone before its first stamp. WP3 owns the set; this WP calls add/delete.
- DatabaseAdapter.ensureRunning?(ref) (WP3 wake door 'explicit start'): basebackup fallback calls it before streaming; reflink never wakes the source.
- Engine.volumeHostPath(project, branch, group): string, used by deployLocked (engine.ts:235) and by WP5 template deploys.
- Engine.migrateLegacyData(): Promise<{ migrated: string[]; skipped: string[]; failed: Array<{ ref: string; error: string }> }> called from main.ts before router/scheduler start; sets engine.booting=true so WP3's sweep is inert until it returns.
- Engine.dataCapabilities(): { dataDir, reflink, engine } for the boot log (WP6 may surface it on the Settings page; no route is added for it).
- Event payload contract: 'branch.created' payload becomes { from, db: { method, ms }, volumes: Array<{ group, method, ms }> } (engine.ts:150); tests and the dashboard Operations page read it.
- Compute destroy/removeComputeService/removeServiceVolume no longer touch docker volumes; they call data.remove on vol paths (engine.ts:833, :1006, compute.ts:41-42).
- LocalPostgres/DockerCompute/LocalManagedDb constructors accept the DataDir (main.ts:19).

algorithm:
A. Boot (src/main.ts, after the docker version check at main.ts:16-17)
1. config = loadConfig(); dataDir = config.dataDir (absolute; realpath if it exists).
2. data.probe():
   a. mkdir -p <dataDir> (mode 0o700) and <dataDir>/.probe.
   b. Write <dataDir>/.probe/src (1 MiB random). fs.copyFileSync(src, dst, fs.constants.COPYFILE_FICLONE_FORCE). Success => reflink=true. ENOTSUP / EXDEV / EINVAL / EOPNOTSUPP => reflink=false. Any other error is thrown (unwritable data dir = fatal, exit 1). Remove both files. Node's FICLONE_FORCE maps to ioctl(FICLONE) on Linux and clonefile/COPYFILE_CLONE_FORCE on macOS, so one probe covers both platforms.
   c. engine = (process.platform === 'darwin' || process.getuid?.() === 0) ? 'inprocess' : 'helper'. Rationale: PGDATA is chowned to uid 999 mode 0700 by the image entrypoint on every start (postgres:16-alpine docker-entrypoint.sh lines 41 and 58, verified), so an unprivileged Linux daemon cannot read it; on macOS Docker Desktop (virtiofs) bind-mount files appear owned by the host user, so the daemon can. 'helper' means the copy/remove programs run inside `docker run --rm -i -v <dataDir>:<dataDir> <helperImage> node - <argv>` with src/fsclone.cjs on stdin (docker() already supports `input`, src/docker.ts:6-20). FICLONE works through a bind mount of the same filesystem, so reflink capability is identical in both engines.
   d. If INSTA_OSS_FORK==='reflink' and reflink===false: exit 1 with 'INSTA_OSS_FORK=reflink but <dataDir> does not support reflinks'. Otherwise log one line: `data dir <path> reflink=<yes|no> engine=<inprocess|helper> mode=<local|server>`; when reflink=false in server mode add 'branch forks will stream pg_basebackup (O(data)); re-run the installer to get an XFS reflink volume'.
3. migrateLegacyData() (section F) unless INSTA_OSS_DATA_MIGRATE=0. Then WP2/WP3 start, then listen.

B. Layout and directory rules (src/datadir.ts)
- pgDir(ref, key='db') = <dataDir>/pg/<ref>/<key>; volDir(ref, volId) = <dataDir>/vol/<ref>/<volId>; mdDir(ref, type, dataId) = <dataDir>/md/<ref>/<MANAGED_DB[type].idPrefix>-<dataId>; branchRoots(ref) = [<dataDir>/pg/<ref>, <dataDir>/vol/<ref>, <dataDir>/md/<ref>].
- ensureDir(path, mode): mkdir -p; chmod to mode. Postgres dirs 0o700 (the entrypoint re-chmods anyway); volume dirs 0o777 (a user image may run as any uid, e.g. n8n as uid 1000 writing N8N_USER_FOLDER=/data, templates/n8n/insta.template.yaml:25-28; a fresh bind mount is not initialised with the image's ownership the way a named volume is; the parent tree is 0700 root in server mode so 0777 leaves nothing exposed); managed dirs 0o700 (all three images chown their data path at start when run as root; our redis command runs as root, src/manageddb.ts:29-32).
- Guards (safety against docker auto-creating a missing bind source as an empty dir): before `docker run/create` with a pg mount, provision requires assertEmptyOrMissing(dir) and every other start/fork requires hasPgData(dir) (PG_VERSION exists); a failed guard throws `data directory <path> is missing PG_VERSION; refusing to start postgres on an empty directory` and never initdb's over a lost mount.
- remove(path): rm -rf in-process; on EACCES (helper engine) run `fsclone.cjs rm <path>` in the helper container. Idempotent (ENOENT ok). Never removes anything outside <dataDir> (path.resolve check).

C. Postgres provision (src/adapters/postgres.ts, replaces :12-20)
1. dir = opts.dataDir; assertEmptyOrMissing(dir); ensureDir(dir, 0o700).
2. docker run -d --restart unless-stopped --name io-<ref>-pg --network <net> -v <dir>:/var/lib/postgresql/data -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=insta -e POSTGRES_DB=app postgres:16-alpine -c shared_preload_libraries=pg_stat_statements. (WP3 may add --stop-timeout; the image already sets STOPSIGNAL SIGINT = fast shutdown, verified.)
3. waitReady(ref, 120 s): loop every 500 ms: `docker exec <c> pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5432 -U postgres -d app` must exit 0, THEN `docker exec <c> psql -h 127.0.0.1 -U postgres -d app -tAc 'select 1'` must print 1. Both use TCP because the image's init-time temporary server listens on the unix socket only (listen_addresses=''), which is exactly why the socket-based pg_isready at postgres.ts:39 reports ready before the final server exists (#34). A container that exits during the loop (docker inspect .State.Status = exited) ends the loop with the last 40 log lines in the error.
4. hba: `docker exec <c> sh -c "grep -q 'insta-oss basebackup' /var/lib/postgresql/data/pg_hba.conf || printf '%s\\n' 'host replication all all scram-sha-256  # insta-oss basebackup' >> /var/lib/postgresql/data/pg_hba.conf"` then query 'select pg_reload_conf()'. Needed because initdb's pg_hba only allows replication over the socket/loopback and the image's `host all all all` line does not match the replication pseudo-database; pg_basebackup from another container would be refused without it. Clones inherit the file.
5. return { url: postgres://postgres:insta@<host>:5432/app } where <host> comes from the same helper WP2 uses for the branch DB hostname (today io-<ref>-pg, postgres.ts:19).

D. Postgres fork (LocalPostgres.fork(src, dst)); engine wraps it with opsInFlight add/delete for both refs
Inputs: src.dataDir (must pass hasPgData), src.url (live credentials), dst.dataDir (assertEmptyOrMissing), dst.network.
1. method selection: forced by INSTA_OSS_FORK, else reflink iff probe.reflink.
2. REFLINK PATH
   a. If the source container is running: query(src.ref, 'CHECKPOINT') (superuser; forces all dirty pages to disk so every later page image differs from WAL only by records that follow the checkpoint; full_page_writes is on by default, so any torn page copied mid-write is restored from WAL). If the source is stopped ('exited'/'created'): skip; its files are at rest (fast shutdown or crash state), no wake. If CHECKPOINT fails because the server stopped between the check and the call, treat as at rest.
   b. t0 = now; data.clonePostgres(srcDir, dstDir), which runs fsclone.cjs `clone --pg --reflink=always`:
      i.   mkdir dst 0700. Copy src/global/pg_control -> dst/.pg_control.fork with a plain read/write (8 KiB) FIRST. This freezes the checkpoint pointer at the forced checkpoint C0 whose redo point precedes every file copy that follows; a pg_control taken later could point at a checkpoint whose redo point is after a data file we already copied, and recovery would then skip that file's changes.
      ii.  Walk every top-level entry of src except pg_wal, in readdir order, recursively: dirs -> mkdir + (after contents) chmod + lchown(if uid 0) + utimes; regular files -> copyFile(COPYFILE_FICLONE_FORCE) then chmod/lchown/utimes; symlinks -> readlink + symlink + lchown (pg_tblspc entries); other types skipped. An ENOTSUP/EXDEV from FICLONE_FORCE aborts with exit code 75 (NoReflink) so the adapter can fall back.
      iii. Copy pg_wal LAST, same walker. Order matters: every WAL record for a change made to a data file after that file was copied is now in the copy; replay is idempotent by page LSN. The segment being written is copied mid-write; recovery stops at the first invalid record, which is the end of WAL as far as the clone knows.
      iv.  Move dst/.pg_control.fork over dst/global/pg_control (rename, atomic).
      v.   Scrub the pg_basebackup exclusion list on dst: empty the directories pg_dynshmem, pg_notify, pg_replslot, pg_serial, pg_snapshots, pg_stat_tmp, pg_subtrans (keep the dirs); delete postmaster.pid, postmaster.opts, backup_label.old, tablespace_map.old, and every pg_internal.init under base/*/ and global/. pg_replslot removal keeps the clone from retaining WAL for the source's slots; postmaster.pid removal avoids any 'lock file already exists' path.
      vi.  fsclone.cjs prints JSON { files, bytes, ms } on stdout.
   c. docker run the clone exactly like provision step 2 with -v dstDir and --name io-<dst>-pg on dst.network (initdb is skipped by the image because PGDATA is non-empty; the source's password, postgresql.conf, postgresql.auto.conf and pg_hba travel with the files).
   d. waitReady(dst.ref, 120 s) as in C.3. Postgres performs crash recovery from C0 to end of WAL (1 to 3 s typical).
   e. Failure classification from `docker logs --tail 200`: if it matches /could not locate a valid checkpoint record|invalid checkpoint record|requested WAL segment .* has already been removed|database files are incompatible/ the copy window overlapped a checkpoint that recycled WAL (possible only if another checkpoint completed during the copy: max_wal_size 1 GB of new WAL or checkpoint_timeout 5 min after our forced one). Then: rm -f -v the container, data.remove(dstDir), retry the reflink path once (new CHECKPOINT), and on a second failure go to the BASEBACKUP PATH. Any other readiness failure (container exited for another reason) is thrown after cleanup.
   f. return { url: src.url with host replaced by the dst host, method: 'reflink', ms: now - t0 }.
3. BASEBACKUP PATH (reflink unsupported, NoReflink exit, or forced)
   a. ensureRunning(src.ref) (WP3 wake door; explicit op, not traffic) then waitReady(src.ref).
   b. Re-run the hba step C.4 on the source (idempotent; covers migrated legacy containers).
   c. ensureDir(dstDir, 0o700). t0 = now. docker run --rm --network <src network> -v <dstDir>:/out -e PGPASSWORD=<password parsed from src.url> postgres:16-alpine pg_basebackup -h io-<src>-pg -p 5432 -U postgres -D /out -X stream --checkpoint=fast --no-password. The image entrypoint execs any non-postgres command as root, so it writes into the bind mount directly; the daemon never buffers a byte. The src network is the branch network `io-<src ref>` (engine.ts:49); WP2's in-network alias also works but the container name is what resolves today (engine.ts:238).
   d. On success: dst has backup_label and its own pg_wal from streaming; delete nothing. Continue with 2.c and 2.d (start, TCP readiness; recovery replays to the backup end point).
   e. On failure: data.remove(dstDir), throw `pg_basebackup failed: <stderr tail>`.
   f. return { url as above, method: 'basebackup', ms }.
4. Password parity: the clone inherits the source's current password (a rotated one from dbSetPassword, engine.ts:1067-1076, included), so the URL is derived from src.url, not from the provision constant; the engine sets Branch.dbUrl to the returned url.
5. Retry-on-connect in query(): wrap the docker exec; on stderr matching the connect-phase set (see files entry) retry with 500 ms backoff until a 30 s deadline; on any other non-zero exit throw immediately (SQL errors must surface at once, e.g. the 'ghost' database test at test/server.test.ts:21).

E. Volumes (engine.ts) and managed DBs
1. deployLocked (engine.ts:219-235): path = volDir(ref, vol.id); data.ensureDir(path, 0o777); pass volume: { hostPath: path }. compute.ts mounts `-v <hostPath>:/data`. A rename keeps the id (engine.ts:807-810), so nothing on disk moves.
2. createBranch, after provisionBranch and before the redeploy loop: for every group in source.apps with project.computeVolumes[group]: srcPath = volDir(srcRef, id); if it exists: data.cloneTree(srcPath, volDir(dstRef, id)) using fsclone.cjs `clone --reflink=auto` (reflink per file when supported, plain copy otherwise; ownership/mode/mtime preserved; xattrs are not, noted in risks); record { group, method, ms }. If the source dir does not exist (never deployed on that branch) skip. Order: volumes fork BEFORE the clone's containers start, and the source app keeps running (a live copy of an app volume is crash-consistent at best; same promise a VM snapshot gives; documented). The clone's app is then redeployed with the forked path by the existing loop (engine.ts:139-141).
3. removeComputeService (engine.ts:833) and removeServiceVolume (:1006): replace `docker volume rm` with data.remove(volDir(ref, id)) per branch, after the container is gone. compute.destroy no longer lists volumes (compute.ts:41-42); the engine removes <dataDir>/vol/<ref> in teardown.
4. Managed DBs: addManagedService mints dataId = randomUUID().slice(0,8) into the project entry; provisionBranch/addManagedService call managedDb.provision(..., { dataDir: mdDir(ref, type, dataId) }) after ensureDir 0o700; the adapter mounts each catalog dataPath `-v <dataDir>/<sub>:<containerPath>`. Branch clones still get a FRESH instance and password (engine.ts:79-89 unchanged; cloud parity insta-platform services.ts:873-874). removeManagedService and teardown remove mdDir / <dataDir>/md/<ref>. renameManagedService stays `docker rename` only (adapters/manageddb.ts:22-25) because the dir key is dataId.

F. Legacy migration (src/datadir-migrate.ts), one-time, at boot, per branch with dataVersion undefined
For each such branch (project ref from engine.ref, engine.ts:45-48), sequentially, with engine.booting=true:
1. Postgres: c = io-<ref>-pg. If the container does not exist: skip pg (nothing to move; the row keeps its legacy mark for this resource but a missing container is treated as done). Else: wasRunning = inspect .State.Running; docker stop c (SIGINT fast shutdown, default 10 s grace); target = pgDir(ref); if hasPgData(target) already (a previous partial run) skip the copy; else data.copyFromContainerVolume(c, '/var/lib/postgresql/data', target) = `docker run --rm --volumes-from c -v <dataDir>:<dataDir> <helperImage> node - clone /var/lib/postgresql/data <target> --reflink=auto` (fsclone.cjs on stdin; runs as root inside, so ownership 999 is preserved; plain copy since the volume lives on docker's own filesystem, which on macOS is inside the VM and unreachable from the host, which is why this is always a container copy); verify PG_VERSION; docker rm -f -v c (drops the anonymous volume); re-create with provision step C.2 using the same args (the bind mount is non-empty so initdb is skipped); if wasRunning: waitReady then hba step C.4; else docker stop it again immediately after readiness (a never-started create is not possible for pg). 
2. Compute volumes: for each group with a volume record and an app on this branch: v = io-<ref>-data-<id> (engine.ts:235); if `docker volume inspect v` fails skip; target = volDir(ref, id); if target is non-empty skip the copy else `docker run --rm -v v:/src:ro -v <dataDir>:<dataDir> <helperImage> node - clone /src <target> --reflink=auto`; then deployLocked(projectId, branchId, group, { image, port, hostPort }) which recreates the container with the bind mount and preserves desiredState (engine.ts:231-255); then docker volume rm v.
3. Managed DBs: for each project.managedServices entry: assign dataId if missing (mutate); c = managedContainerName(ref, type, name); if absent skip; stop; for each catalog dataPath copy via --volumes-from into mdDir(...)/<sub>; rm -f -v; re-provision with the SAME password (branch.managed[id].password) and the new mount; restore run state.
4. mutate: branches[id].dataVersion = 1 only when every resource of the branch is migrated; otherwise log the failure list and continue with the next branch (boot never blocks; the branch keeps working on docker volumes; createBranch from a legacy source throws `branch <name> still stores data in docker volumes; restart the daemon to retry the migration`, and WP3 treats a legacy branch like any other because it addresses containers by name).
5. Result is logged once: migrated/skipped/failed counts and per-failure reasons. Idempotent and resumable: every step checks the target before copying and the old resource before removing.

G. Teardown (engine.ts:1141-1169)
destroyBranch/destroyProject: compute.destroy (rm -f -v), db.destroy (rm -f -v), storage.destroy (unchanged), managed destroys (rm -f -v), network rm, THEN data.remove for each of branchRoots(ref) (in-process, helper on EACCES), then the state mutation. A remove failure is logged and does not fail the delete (the state row is gone; a later boot sweeps orphan dirs under <dataDir>/{pg,vol,md} whose ref matches no branch, logging each, never deleting a dir whose ref still exists in state).

H. Copy engine selection per call (DataDir)
try in-process; if the error is EACCES or EPERM and platform is linux: run the same verb in the helper container (one docker run per verb; the pull of node:22-alpine happens once). Anything else propagates. In-process is the normal path in server mode (root in the daemon container) and on macOS.

I. Timing targets (measured by test/fork.int.test.ts through the branch.created payload)
- reflink: clonePostgres ms <= 2000 for a 1 GiB PGDATA (about 1.5k files), <= 5000 at 10 GiB; end-to-end createBranch database step (copy + container start + recovery + TCP ready) <= 10 s; size independence: ms(200 MiB) / ms(20 MiB) < 3.
- basebackup: about 10 to 20 s per GiB on a VPS disk; the test asserts < 60 s for 200 MiB.
- Local-mode caveat: on macOS Docker Desktop the copy is host-side clonefile (sub-second) but container start over virtiofs adds 1 to 2 s.

CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml): the XFS loop-mount step makes the ubuntu runner exercise the reflink path (probe must report reflink=true; the fork test asserts it when INSTA_OSS_EXPECT_REFLINK=1), and a second invocation with INSTA_OSS_FORK=basebackup exercises the fallback. Because the runner user is not root, this also exercises the helper engine (node:22-alpine) on Linux. Docker test files keep distinct project names (forktest, migtest, citest, sttest, restartint) since vitest runs files in parallel (vitest.config.ts:5); implementers never run Docker tests concurrently with each other.
risks: Cloud divergence: the cloud gives a branch a FRESH EMPTY /data volume (insta-platform src/provisioning/branch.ts:283-285, docs/projects/branches.mdx:17), self-host will fork it. Allowed under decision 1 (daemon-internal behaviour), but the docs table needs a self-host column and the skill's divergence list gains one line.

Reflink copy window: pg_control is frozen at the forced checkpoint C0; if another checkpoint completes during the copy (needs max_wal_size = 1 GB of new WAL or checkpoint_timeout = 5 min) the WAL from C0 may be recycled and the clone fails to start. Mitigated by detection + one retry + basebackup fallback; not eliminated. Raising wal_keep_size per branch would widen the window at a per-branch disk cost and is deliberately not done.
Node copy does not preserve xattrs/ACLs (no Node API); PGDATA has none, user volumes rarely do (file capabilities on binaries under /data would be lost). Documented, not mitigated.
Unprivileged Linux local mode depends on pulling node:22-alpine (~50 MB) once for copies and removals; the pull needs network. Server mode and macOS never need it.

macOS Docker Desktop: Postgres on a virtiofs bind mount is supported but slower than a named volume (fsync-heavy workloads); reflink probe on the host says yes (APFS) while FICLONE inside the VM would say no, so the copy MUST run in-process on macOS (the engine rule guarantees this). INSTA_OSS_DATA_DIR must live under a Docker Desktop shared path.

Migration restarts every legacy container once (stop, copy, recreate) on the first boot after upgrade: minutes of downtime per GB on a laptop with many branches; partial failures leave a branch on docker volumes and unforkable until a retry. The boot log and the thrown message say so.
pg_basebackup needs the extra pg_hba replication line; a user who hand-edits pg_hba and drops it breaks only the fallback, and the adapter re-appends it before each fallback.

Volume fork of a running app is crash-consistent, not application-consistent (SQLite WAL files inside /data are fine; a mid-write of a large file may be torn). Same class of promise as a disk snapshot; documented.

Reflink clones make `du` under-report per-branch disk (blocks are shared until modified); the dashboard's advisory sizes (engine.ts:14-17) are unaffected, but an operator watching free space should trust `df`, not `du`. A full XFS loop image makes Postgres PANIC on write; installer sizing (WP1) and a free-space warning in the boot log are the mitigations.

Ownership: fresh volume dirs are 0777 so any container uid can write; acceptable only because the parent tree is 0700 root (server mode) or the user's home (local); the installer must not relax <dataDir> permissions.

Bind-mount hazard: docker recreates a missing bind source as an empty dir on start; guarded for Postgres (PG_VERSION check) but a manually deleted volume dir would silently come back empty for compute (same as a deleted named volume today).

Orphan sweep at boot deletes dirs whose ref matches no branch; a state.json restored from an older backup could make live data look orphaned. The sweep only logs in v1 and deletes only when INSTA_OSS_SWEEP_ORPHANS=1 (installer never sets it).
openQuestions: Postgres directory key: task text says <dataDir>/pg/<ref>; this design uses <dataDir>/pg/<ref>/<svcKey> with svcKey='db' so the multi-postgres WP (decision 6) slots additional databases in without a second migration. Reconciler to confirm the key the multi-postgres WP mints (must be immutable, not the service name).

Volume directory key: task text says <dataDir>/vol/<ref>/<group>; this design keys by the existing immutable volume id (engine.ts:780, :807-810) so `insta services rename compute` never moves a bind source. Confirm.

Should the `empty: true` field of the cloud's createBranch (openapi.yaml:3860-3866) be honoured now that forks are cheap? Today server.ts:181 ignores it. It belongs to whichever WP reshapes project/branch services (decision 6); WP4's fork code is unaffected either way.

Clone sleep policy: spec section 5.6 says a new branch's compute sleeps immediately unless alwaysOn; should the forked database also be stopped right after readiness (it costs ~50 MB RSS idle) or get the normal idle window? WP3 decision; WP4 leaves it running with a fresh stamp.

Helper image choice: node:22-alpine keeps one copy program; if WP1's daemon image is itself node:22-alpine the helper could be `ghcr.io/insforge/instacloud` in server mode, but server mode never needs the helper (root in-process). Confirm node:22-alpine is acceptable as the only image pulled for unprivileged Linux local mode.
Should legacy migration also run lazily (on first fork of a legacy branch) rather than only at boot? Design says boot-only with a clear error; lazy would add a wake + copy inside a user request.
Docs ownership: WP6 owns docs/, but the three branching pages assert 'dump-and-restore' and 'volume empty' for self-host; WP4 lists the exact lines to change so the reconciler can assign them.
dependsOn: WP1 (packaging/install): the reflink filesystem at <dataDir>, mode 0700 root, mounted at the same path inside the daemon container, daemon uid 0 in server mode, compose mounting the docker socket; src/config.ts fields INSTA_OSS_MODE and INSTA_OSS_DATA_DIR.

WP2 (router/hostnames): the branch DB host helper used to build clone URLs (fork swaps only the host in the source URL); no other coupling. The basebackup path dials the source by container name on the branch network, which works before and after WP2.

WP3 (scheduler): opsInFlight set (fork marks src+dst), DatabaseAdapter.ensureRunning wake seam for the basebackup path, engine.booting flag honoured by the sweep during migration, and the compute stop-with-grace change (not needed by WP4 but the same adapter file).
Multi-postgres / empty project WP (decision 6): must mint immutable svcKeys for pg/<ref>/<svcKey> and call provision/fork per postgres service; WP4's single fixed 'db' key is forward compatible.
